detail.body:
Add a new `cpp` language pack alongside the existing MVP packs.

This gives users a C++ option for generating bugs, viewing mocked
snippets, and falling back to canned examples when generation is
exhausted. The pack is registered as a built-in, documented in the
README and language-pack guide, and covered by smoke tests so the new
config id behaves like the other shipped packs.

The web UI now recognizes C++ syntax for code highlighting, so generated
snippets remain readable in the browser when the `cpp` pack is selected.

Add Rust as a supported language pack alongside the existing Swift,
JavaScript, and Python packs.

This gives the app a Rust MVP curriculum, including scenario seeds,
mock snippets, canned fallbacks, and mix/category definitions so Rust
can be selected in config and exercised in tests.

The UI highlighter now understands Rust syntax, and the documentation
and README list Rust as an available pack for users and contributors.

Python is now a first-class MVP pack alongside Swift and JavaScript.
Users can select `game.languagepack: python` and get Python scenarios,
fallback snippets, and mock content with Python-aware highlighting.

This expands the available curriculum for the Python track and keeps
offline UI work, config validation, and pack registration consistent
with the existing built-in packs. Registry, config, and smoke tests
cover the new pack so it loads and generates correctly.
